[#29387](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/29387#issuecomment-954769602) was closed because there didn't exist a `ReadOnlySet` at the time. Now that it exists, will that also come in .Net 9? I didn't see it in the closing PR (#103306).

review_comments: Similar to `SyncRoot`, shouldn't this forward to the `ICollection` implementation if available?
This is following what both ReadOnlyCollection and ReadOnlyDictionary do here.

Do you know why? It seems arguably wrong in those cases too.

Of course, hopefully nobody's writing new code that uses this property.

> Do you know why?

I don't. But it's been that way for over a decade, I've not heard anyone complain ever, these members are legacy and discouraged from use, and this isn't a place to innovate (especially since there's no built-in set for which IsSynchronized is true). If you believe it's buggy and worth fixing, we can handle that for all of them as part of a separate issue you open, but this type shouldn't differ from those existing ones, and I don't think it's appropriate to change those other types as part of this PR adding a new type.
Could you add a test checking that post-hoc mutations to the underlying set are reflected by the read-only wrapper?
Should this be able to use `HashSet<T>.Empty`?

indeed, it was a question for @stephentoub - is that intentionally missing, or should we add it? I'm assuming it's an intentional decision to not have it on any mutable collections, although we do have it in some places eg., XmlDictionary.

We intentionally do not have it on mutable collections. Empty would return a singleton `HashSet<T>`, which could then be mutated and no longer be empty.

(XmlDictionary.Empty doesn't return XmlDictionary, it returns IXmlDictionary. It was defined 20+ years ago and breaks from our desired pattern of Empty returning the same type on which it is declared.)
